newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU proposes bus safety standards.
newsitem.headline: EU proposes bus safety standards.

text.p: The European Commission proposed on Wednesday new safety standards for buses in areas ranging from distribution of passenger weight to access to emergency exits.
The legislation would allow Britain and Ireland, however, to evade certain requirements that would pose technical problems for double-decker, mini- and midi-buses.
The proposal aims to ensure that vehicles that are approved in one European Union country can be sold across the EU without further red tape.
"Until now, technical requirements for buses and coaches have been laid down in national legislation," the Commission said in a statement.

The legislation, which must be approved by the European Parliament and EU ministers, covers the number and arrangement of service doors and emergency exits, technical requirements for doors, the size and spacing of seats, vehicle stability and body structure strength.
It also would require vehicles used for urban services to be accessible to people in wheelchairs.
The Commission said EU states could decide not to apply certain provisions to double decker, mini- or midi-buses -- for example, minimum seat widths of 45 centimetres for minibuses.
However, other EU states could bar those vehicles from their territories.
